issues.title: Ensure only notification managers/sys admins can see/use pencil on notification responses page
issues.description:
## Story

Today only Notification Managers can use the manual edit-response feature. This should be broadened so System Administrators can also use it (even when they have not been assigned the Notification Manager role). The pencil edit icon must be hidden from all other users, and any user without one of those two roles who attempts to access the edit-response URL directly must be redirected back to the notification index page.

## Acceptance Criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Edit-response access broadened to Notification Managers and System Administrators

  Scenario: Notification Manager sees the pencil and can open the edit form
    Given I am logged in as a Notification Manager (without the System Administrator role)
    And I am viewing the notification event response tracking page
    When the responses table is rendered
    Then I see the pencil edit icon next to each response row
    And clicking the pencil opens the edit-response form for that row
    And submitting the form saves the manual response successfully

  Scenario: System Administrator sees the pencil and can open the edit form
    Given I am logged in as a System Administrator (without the Notification Manager role)
    And I am viewing the notification event response tracking page
    When the responses table is rendered
    Then I see the pencil edit icon next to each response row
    And clicking the pencil opens the edit-response form for that row
    And submitting the form saves the manual response successfully

  Scenario: User with both Notification Manager and System Administrator roles can edit
    Given I am logged in as a user with both the Notification Manager and System Administrator roles
    And I am viewing the notification event response tracking page
    Then I see the pencil edit icon next to each response row
    And the edit-response form is accessible and savable

  Scenario: Supervisor cannot see the pencil
    Given I am logged in as a Supervisor (without the Notification Manager or System Administrator role)
    And I am viewing the notification event response tracking page
    When the responses table is rendered
    Then the pencil edit icon is not present on any row

  Scenario: Supervisor attempting to access the edit-response URL is redirected
    Given I am logged in as a Supervisor (without the Notification Manager or System Administrator role)
    When I navigate directly to the edit-response URL for a known response
    Then I am redirected to the notification index page with an error indicator

  Scenario: Regular user cannot see the pencil
    Given I am logged in as a user with no Notification Manager or System Administrator role
    And I have somehow reached the notification event response tracking page
    When the responses table is rendered
    Then the pencil edit icon is not present on any row

  Scenario: Regular user attempting to access the edit-response URL is redirected
    Given I am logged in as a user with no Notification Manager or System Administrator role
    When I navigate directly to the edit-response URL for a known response
    Then I am redirected to the notification index page with an error indicator

```

issues.title: Add EmployeeId-only employee upload + include EmployeeId in existing ProcessRaw
issues.description:
## Background A customer has asked for a new file-upload workflow that matches existing employee by **PersonaId** and **only** updates their **EmployeeId**. This is a lighter-weight complement to the full employee CSV upload at `~/setting/customer/process/` ([Upload.cshtml](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Customer/Views/Customer/Upload.cshtml)) so customers can backfill EmployeeIds without re-sending the entire employee roster. In addition, the existing employee CSV upload (`ORBIT.Model.Employee.ProcessRaw` at [Employee.cs:1253](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Employee/Employee.cs#L1253)) needs to learn a new optional `EmployeeId` column so future full uploads can carry the value in one pass. > **Note:** `EmployeeId` is the same value as **Employee ID**. Employee are currently keyed by `PersonaId`; the system is mid-migration toward `EmployeeId`. This work should populate `EmployeeId` cleanly so the eventual Employee ID cutover has the data it needs. --- ## Scope ### 1. New "EmployeeId Upload" workflow (PersonaId → EmployeeId only) **Model — `ORBIT.Model.Employee`** - Add a new static method, e.g. `Employee.ProcessEmployeeIdRaw( Customer customer, Stream stream )`, mirroring the streaming/parsing pattern of `ProcessRaw` (TextFieldParser, `stream.Length > 100` early-exit, batched `Parallel.ForEach` over `csvList.Chunk( 250 )`). - Expected CSV columns (in order): 1. PersonaId 2. EmployeeId - For each row: - `Employee existing = Employee.FetchBy( uniqueId: personaId );` scoped to the supplied customer. - If found and `EmployeeId` is non-empty, update **only** the `EmployeeId` field. Reuse the targeted update path already in `Employee.cs` ([Employee.cs:3358](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Employee/Employee.cs#L3358)) — `Builders.Update.Set( t => t.EmployeeId, employeeId )` and `ORBIT.Model.Queue.Employee.UpdateEmployeeIdToSql( ... )` — so we don't trigger a full `Save()` (which would re-write all encrypted fields and emit unrelated SQL queue noise). - If `existing` is null, log a SystemLog warning (`PersonaId not found for customer X`) and skip — do **not** create new employee from this upload. - Encrypt the value the same way `Employee.Save()` does today before writing. **Controller — `ORBIT.Web.Areas.Customer.Controllers.CustomerController`** - Add a sibling action to `Process(...)` ([CustomerController.cs:210](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Customer/Controllers/CustomerController.cs#L210)), e.g. `ProcessEmployeeId( Model.Customer customer )`, that copies the upload stream and dispatches `Employee.ProcessEmployeeIdRaw` on a background `Task.Run` just like `Process` does today. Redirect back to the customer view with a `?working=1` / `?error=1` query flag. **View** - Add a new view alongside [Upload.cshtml](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Customer/Views/Customer/Upload.cshtml), e.g. `UploadEmployeeId.cshtml`, modeled on Upload.cshtml with: - `form action="~/setting/customer/processemployeeid/"` - A single file input bound to `FileEmployeeImport` (reuse the existing property on `CustomerViewModel` / `Customer`). - Instructions section listing the two-column format (Persona ID, EmployeeId). - Wire a link/button on the customer view page to reach the new upload. ### 2. Add `EmployeeId` to the existing employee upload (`ProcessRaw`) - Extend the column contract of `Employee.ProcessRaw` to **append** a new optional column at the end (avoid renumbering the 12 existing columns to keep customer files backward-compatible): - **12 - EmployeeId** *(optional, may be blank)* - Update both the create branch ([Employee.cs:1407-1439](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Employee/Employee.cs#L1407-L1439)) and the update branch (lines immediately following) to populate `EmployeeId` when the column is present and non-empty. When blank, leave the existing value untouched on update (do **not** wipe an already-set EmployeeId). - Defensive bounds-check on `row.Length` so old 12-column files still parse. - Update the in-source column comment block at [Employee.cs:1269-1282](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Employee/Employee.cs#L1269-L1282). - Update [Upload.cshtml](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Customer/Views/Customer/Upload.cshtml) Instructions list to add `
  • EmployeeId (optional)
    • ` after Position Title. --- ## Files to touch | File | Change | |---|---| | [Employee.cs](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Employee/Employee.cs) | Add `ProcessEmployeeIdRaw`; extend `ProcessRaw` for optional EmployeeId column | | [CustomerController.cs](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Customer/Controllers/CustomerController.cs) | Add `ProcessEmployeeId` action | | Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Customer/Views/Customer/UploadEmployeeId.cshtml | New view | | [Upload.cshtml](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Customer/Views/Customer/Upload.cshtml) | Add EmployeeId to instruction list | | Customer view page | Link to new upload | > ⚠️ `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Employee/` is normally off-limits in routine refactors; this work intentionally requires edits there because the upload logic lives in `Employee.cs`. --- ## Test plan - **Unit (`ORBIT.Test.Unit`):** Mirror [EmployeeProcessRaw.cs](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Test.Unit/Employee/EmployeeProcessRaw.cs): - `ProcessEmployeeIdRaw` early-exits on null / tiny streams. - `ProcessEmployeeIdRaw` updates EmployeeId for an existing PersonaId (try/finally restores original EmployeeId; clean up `ORBIT.Model.Queue.Employee` per the project convention). - `ProcessEmployeeIdRaw` no-ops for an unknown PersonaId (logs only, no new Employee created). - `ProcessRaw` continues to parse a 12-column file unchanged (regression). - `ProcessRaw` populates EmployeeId from a new 13-column file. - `ProcessRaw` leaves an existing EmployeeId alone when column 12 is blank on update. - **Manual / Playwright:** Upload a sample 2-column CSV from the new customer view link, confirm EmployeeId appears on Employee form. Upload a 13-column employee CSV, confirm EmployeeId populates. --- ## Out of scope - The broader PersonaId → Employee ID partition-key migration. - Bulk EmployeeId backfill from any external/authoritative source.

issues.title: Backfill unit tests for Helper namespace
issues.description:
**Goal:** Close the single largest unit-test gap in the codebase — the `ORBIT.Model.Helper` namespace has 33 classes and ~119 public methods with **zero** tests today. These are mostly pure functions, so they are the highest test-per-hour return on the board.

**Scope:** All classes under `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Helper/`, including (non-exhaustive):
- `StringEncryption` — AES round-trip, key handling
- `Extension` (string / DateTime / collection extensions)
- `Email` — format validation, normalization
- `PhoneNumber` — parse, format, mask
- `UniqueId` — generation, uniqueness
- `Enumeration` — enum helpers
- `BsonExtensions` — to/from BSON conversions
- `DateExtensions` — UTC normalization, business-day math

**What will be done:**
1. Create a test file per logical grouping under `Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Test.Unit/Helper/`:
   - `Helper_Encryption.cs`
   - `Helper_StringExtensions.cs`
   - `Helper_PhoneNumber.cs`
   - `Helper_DateExtensions.cs`
   - `Helper_BsonExtensions.cs`
   - `Helper_Email.cs`
   - `Helper_UniqueId.cs`
   - `Helper_Enumeration.cs`
2. Cover happy path, boundary cases (null / empty / max length), and any round-trip invariants (encrypt/decrypt, BSON-serialize/deserialize).
3. Follow project test conventions — no DB dependency required for most of these; `Assert.Inconclusive` only where helpers reach external resources.
4. Lift unit-method coverage from ~70% (of tested classes) toward ~80% overall.

**Out of scope:** Helpers under `ORBIT.Web/` (those belong with controller tests).

issues.title: Fix System Log search returning no results
issues.description:
## Summary

The System Log search UI (`/application/log/`) returns no results for any query, even though the initial table populates correctly. Search has historically been very useful for investigating issues, so this needs to be fixed.

## Root cause

There is a field-name mismatch between how `SystemLog` records are written and how `Log<T>.Search` queries them.

### Where the data is written

[`Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/SystemLog.cs` lines 18–33](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/SystemLog.cs#L18-L33) — every `SystemLog` constructor sets the `ApplicationLogType` property (serialized to the Mongo field `ApplicationLogType`). A grep across the codebase confirms nothing ever sets `SystemLogType` on a `SystemLog` (only `Ooo.cs` sets it, and that is a different collection). So every `SystemLog` document in Mongo looks like:

- `ApplicationLogType` = 1, 2, ... (one of the valid enum values)
- `SystemLogType` = 0  ← default value from the base-class property; not a valid enum entry

### Where the search queries it

[`Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/Log.cs` lines 82–94](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/Log.cs#L82-L94) — `Log<T>.Search` builds an `$and` of two `$or` clauses. The second clause is:

```csharp
filterBuilder.Or(
    filterBuilder.Eq( "SystemLogType", SystemLogType.Exception ),            // 1
    filterBuilder.Eq( "SystemLogType", SystemLogType.Information ),          // 2
    filterBuilder.Eq( "SystemLogType", SystemLogType.EmployeeInactive ),    // 9
    filterBuilder.Eq( "SystemLogType", SystemLogType.EmployeeNotRegistered )// 10
)
```

No `SystemLog` document has `SystemLogType` in `{1, 2, 9, 10}` — every document has `SystemLogType = 0` — so the filter matches zero rows on every query. That is why search always returns "No records were returned" while `FetchRecent()` (no type filter, [`Log.cs` lines 58–67](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/Log.cs#L58-L67)) still populates the initial table correctly.

## Fix options

1. Change the secondary `$or` in `Log<T>.Search` to filter on the field the records actually use (`"ApplicationLogType"` with the corresponding `ApplicationLogType` enum values). Preserves original intent of restricting to user-facing categories.
2. Drop the secondary `$or` entirely — `FetchRecent` already returns everything without a type filter, and the search endpoint at [`JsonController.cs` line 767](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/JsonController.cs#L767) is already gated to system administrators.

Option 1 is the more conservative change.

issues.title: Audit-log individual check-in reminder emails sent from the home page
issues.description:
## Summary

When a supervisor or manager sends an individual employee check-in reminder email from the home page, we currently have no audit trail. We need to log **who** initiated the reminder, **who** it was sent to, and **when**, so we can investigate disputes and confirm what was actually sent.

## Where this happens today

[`Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/HomeController.cs` `SendReminder(string id)` lines 378–463](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/HomeController.cs#L378-L463).

Two code paths exist in this action:

1. **No `id` provided** — bulk send to every unreported employee under the supervisor/manager's roles. Sends happen on a background `Task.Run`, looping `Reminder.SendReminderFromSupervisor(p.Email)` per person ([lines 420–438](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/HomeController.cs#L420-L438)).
2. **`id` provided** — single individual send. Calls `Reminder.SendReminderFromSupervisor(employee.Email)` directly ([lines 444–450](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/HomeController.cs#L444-L450)).

Neither path writes an audit record on the success path. Only thrown exceptions are logged to `SystemLog` ([line 432, line 456](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/HomeController.cs#L432)). The same gap exists in the sibling `SendReminderSupervised()` action just below ([lines 465–525](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/HomeController.cs#L465-L525)) — should be addressed in the same change for consistency.

## What to log

At minimum, for every reminder sent (both bulk and individual paths):

- **Sender** — identity of the supervisor/manager initiating (from `WebSession` — likely PersonaId/Employee ID + display name).
- **Recipient** — Employee identity and email address actually sent to.
- **Timestamp** — when the send was initiated (UTC).
- **Initiation context** — which action (`SendReminder` individual, `SendReminder` bulk, or `SendReminderSupervised`).
- **Customer** — the customer scope the supervisor was acting in.

## Suggested approach

Add the audit entry inside the loop / single-send branches immediately after `SendReminderFromSupervisor(...)` succeeds (before the `Save()`), and inside the `catch` so failures also produce an audit row tagged as failed. Either:

- Reuse `SystemLog` with a structured message and a dedicated `Source` value so the existing System Logs UI search (once [#1354](../issues/1354) is fixed) can find them; or
- Add a purpose-built `ReminderAuditLog` entity in `ORBIT.Model.Log` if the data warrants its own searchable view.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every individual reminder send writes an audit record on success.
- [ ] Every bulk-send iteration writes a per-recipient audit record on success.
- [ ] Failures continue to be captured (with sender + recipient context, not just the exception).
- [ ] Records are visible / searchable to system administrators.
- [ ] Same coverage applied to `SendReminderSupervised`.

issues.title: Fix Application Response search returning no results
issues.description:
## Summary

The Application Response page at `/setting/application/response/` populates its initial table correctly, but typing any value into the search box returns "No records were returned." Same symptom as [#1354](../issues/1354), but a different root cause.

## Root cause

The page **displays one collection but searches a different one.**

### Where the initial table comes from

- Controller: [`Areas/Application/Controllers/ResponseController.cs` line 17](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Application/Controllers/ResponseController.cs#L17) — `ResponseTime.FetchRecent()`
- Model: [`Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/ResponseTime.cs`](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/ResponseTime.cs) — class `ORBIT.Model.Log.ResponseTime` with fields `Uri`, `Time`, `PersonaId`
- View: [`Areas/Application/Views/Response/Index.cshtml` lines 25–35](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Areas/Application/Views/Response/Index.cshtml#L25-L35) — iterates `Model.ResponseTimeList`, renders `systemResponse.Uri`, `systemResponse.Time`, `systemResponse.PersonaId`

### Where the search hits

- JS handler: [`wwwroot/js/script.js` lines 3447–3505](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/wwwroot/js/script.js#L3447-L3505) — `fieldset[data-search='systemresponse']` POSTs to `/json/search_systemresponse/`
- Controller endpoint: [`Controllers/JsonController.cs` lines 785–801](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/Controllers/JsonController.cs#L785-L801) — `SearchSystemResponse` calls `SystemResponse.SearchBy(searchValue)`
- Model queried: [`Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Application/Response.cs`](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Application/Response.cs) — class `ORBIT.Model.Application.SystemResponse` (fields `Url`, `Time`, `PersonaId`) — a **different MongoDB collection** from `ResponseTime`

So the user sees rows from `ResponseTime` but the search query is run against `SystemResponse`, which is either empty or contains unrelated documents. Result: no matches, ever.

### Bonus issue (same handler)

Even if the right collection were queried, the JS at [`script.js` line 3479](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Web/wwwroot/js/script.js#L3479) renders `systemResponse.AkoId` in the last column — a stale property name from before the PersonaId migration. The corresponding model field is `PersonaId`, so the cell would render `undefined`. Worth fixing in the same change.

## Fix options

1. **Repoint the search at `ResponseTime`** (the collection the page actually shows). Add a `SearchBy` to `ResponseTime` (it already has one — [`ResponseTime.cs` lines 50–84](Source/dotnet/ORBIT.Model/Log/ResponseTime.cs#L50-L84)), update `JsonController.SearchSystemResponse` to call `ResponseTime.SearchBy(searchValue)`, and adjust the JS field mapping (`Uri` instead of `Url`, `PersonaId` instead of `AkoId`).
2. Or, if `SystemResponse` is in fact the intended source going forward, switch `ResponseController.Index` and the view to use `SystemResponse.FetchRecent()` so the displayed and searched collections agree.

Option 1 is the conservative change and keeps the existing data visible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Typing 3+ characters into the search box on `/setting/application/response/` returns matching rows from the same collection shown in the initial table.
- [ ] Persona ID column populates correctly in search results (not `undefined`).
- [ ] Empty/non-matching searches still show the "No records were returned." message.

issues.title: bug: Northeast Region cannot change layer names
bug: Intermittent and random email reminders being sent to DNR
issues.description:
## Summary (corrected root cause)

The "intermittent / random, before‑8:30‑AM‑local" reminders are **manual reminders triggered by supervisors/managers from the Home page** — **not** the scheduler. In the deployed build these manual sends fire on a plain **GET**, are **not logged**, and go to a supervisor's "no location reported" list, which spans time zones — so recipients *west* of the sender receive a "ORBIT - Check-In Reminder" (the same subject the scheduler uses) **before 8:30 their local time**.

> An earlier version of this description blamed the `DateStatus` / "did‑not‑report" time‑zone math. That has been **disproven** (see Evidence) and is not the cause.

## Evidence

- **Scheduler is correctly timed** (exonerated three ways):
  - Per‑person: `DateReminderCheckIn` converted to each recipient's own zone lands at **08:30 / 08:45 local**.
  - 3 weeks of `SystemLog` (`Source = "Reminder.Email.RemindToReport"`) show firing only at the expected UTC slots, with at most a harmless `:31`/`:46` (one‑minute *late*) drift — **never early**.
- **Time‑zone data is clean** — of the reminder‑eligible population only **1** person lacks `IanaTimeZoneId`; `Name`↔`IanaTimeZoneId` are consistent (Eastern↔`America/New_York`, etc.). So mis‑migrated time zones are **not** the cause.
- **The manual path is unlogged in production.** `ORBIT.Web/Controllers/HomeController.cs` `SendReminder` / `SendReminderSupervised` at tag `v3.3.2.0` contain **0** `ReminderLog` writes (logging is being added on the current sprint branch). That is why `ReminderLog` is empty and the early sends were invisible.
- **The manual path is in heavy, cross‑zone use.** `ReminderSentToday` (set only by the manual path; the scheduler uses `DateReminderCheckIn`) was `true` for **214 people today** — 194 Eastern, 19 Central, 1 Pacific. An Eastern manager hitting "remind all" early morning lands on their Central/Pacific reports before those reports' 8:30 local.

## Why it's "accidental"

The Home‑page reminder controls are `<a href>` **GET** links (`~/home/sendreminder/{id}/`, `~/home/sendreminder/`, `~/home/sendremindersupervised/`) and the actions have **no `[HttpPost]`** and **no anti‑forgery**. The JS confirm modal calls `preventDefault()` on click, but that does nothing for a GET issued by **browser prefetch/prerender, a refresh/back, or a misclick / opened‑in‑new‑tab** — any of which fires the send with no human intent. The bulk "remind all" has no server‑side guard.

## Fix

1. Make `SendReminder` / `SendReminderSupervised` **`[HttpPost]` + `[ValidateAntiForgeryToken]`** so a GET (prefetch/refresh/direct) returns 405 and can no longer trigger a send.
2. Submit the deliberate click as a **token‑bearing POST** (confirm modal updated; anti‑forgery token rendered on the page). The existing confirmation dialog is retained.
3. Keep the **`ReminderLog` logging** being added this sprint — it gives ongoing visibility (it does not, by itself, stop the early sends).
4. Optional follow‑ups: a **time‑zone guard** (warn/block when reminding a recipient before ~8:30 their local time) and a **distinct subject/source** so manual vs. scheduled reminders are tellable in inboxes and logs.

## Verify after deploy

Once the new `ReminderLog` logging is live, group today's entries by source + recipient‑local time; expect `Home Page - …` rows landing **before 08:30** for western recipients.

## Notes

- A small hardening was kept from the earlier investigation: `TimeZone.Difference` now guards `FindSystemTimeZoneById` (an invalid `IanaTimeZoneId` previously threw out of the getter and aborted the roll‑call save, making that person a permanent DNR). The rest of that earlier prototype was removed as not relevant to this defect.

issues.title: Matrixed To Org Future check-in issue
issues.description:
When an employee is in an organization (A) and matrixed to another organization (B), there is an issue with future check-in being displayed on the home screen of certain roles. 

Matrixed To (B) Org Manager see the location  as reported

Matrixed to Layer Manager sees the location as reported

issues.title: Fix matrixed-to-supervisor future check-in visibility on Home screen (#1386)
issues.description:
Fix for #1386. A person in org A matrixed to a supervisor in org B showed as "no location reported" on the matrix supervisor's Home screen, while the matrix Org Manager and Layer Manager saw the location correctly.

**Root cause**
The supervisor section built its "reported" list from `CheckInHot.FetchBy(Supervisor)`, which resolved the matrix relationship from the **frozen embedded** `Employee.MatrixSupervisor` snapshot on the roll-call document. The supervised list, by contrast, read the **live** `Employee.MatrixSupervisor`, so a matrixed person appeared in the list but their check-in was filtered out. Managers were unaffected because they match by `MatrixCustomerLayer`, which is reliably present.
